tier1.text: The cell body holds the nucleus, which contains the cell's DNA. Extensions called processes reach out from the cell body, but they are not part of it. Astrocytes, star-shaped cells that support nerve cells, have many processes reaching out from the main cell body. By contrast, an oligodendrocyte, a cell that insulates nerve fibers, has just a few processes.

quotes.quote: One cell providing support to neurons of the CNS is the astrocyte, so named because it appears to be star-shaped under the microscope (astro- = “star”).
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

sentences.text: By contrast, an oligodendrocyte, a cell that insulates nerve fibers, has just a few processes.

quotes.quote: Also found in CNS tissue is the oligodendrocyte, sometimes called just “oligo,” which is the glial cell type that insulates axons in the CNS. The name means “cell of a few branches” (oligo- = “few”; dendro- = “branches”; -cyte = “cell”). There are a few processes that extend from the cell body.
